business_summary.text: Aditya Infotech Limited operates in the security surveillance industry under the CP PLUS brand, providing AI-powered solutions and expanding into new product categories.

call_points.text: Management upped FY27 guidance to ₹6,000-6,500 Cr revenue, 14-15% EBITDA margin, and 8.5-9.5% PAT.
FY27 capex is planned at ₹200-300 Cr, supporting doubling of capacity by 2028.
Housing plant targeting 30 million units per year; Phase-1 operational by Q2FY27 and Phase-2 by Q4FY27.
Low-cost component inventory is exhausted; price increases will be passed on gradually on a monthly basis.
Cash conversion cycle lengthened slightly due to advance payments and buffer inventory for chips and memory.
Entered partnership with L&T Semiconductor Technologies for 9 million CCTV IP cameras over three years.
Raised FY27 revenue guidance to ₹6,000–6,500 Cr from earlier ₹5,350–5,550 Cr.
Raised FY27 EBITDA margin guidance to 14–15% from 12–13% guided earlier.
Upgraded FY27 adjusted PAT margin target to 8.5–9.5% from earlier 7.5–8.5%.
Kadapa plant capacity reached 2.5M units per month; targeting 2X capacity expansion by FY28.
Launched two new brands, Nexivue and Eyra, to drive market share expansion.

penalties.authority: Office of the Deputy State Tax Officer (Roving Squad), Tenkasi
penalties.details: The Company received a penalty notice under Section 129 of the CGST Act, 2017, in Form GST MOV-07 from the State Tax Officer, Roving Squad IV, Chennai, on January 5, 2026, in relation to detention of goods during transit amounting to Rs. 2,40,656/-. The goods were transported with a valid tax invoice and e-way bill; however, they were detained as the “bill-to” address was not reflected in the customer’s GST registration records. To secure release of the goods, the Company deposited penalty of Rs 43,318/- under CGST and Rs 43,318/- under SGST through Form DRC-03 dated January 05, 2026.
penalties.impact: The Company does not expect any material adverse financial impact arising out of the aforesaid matter

penalties.authority: Office of the Assistant Commissioner (Audit), CGST & Central Excise (Audit), Circle-V, 1st Floor, BSNL Telephone Exchange Building Transport Nagar, Indore, M.P.-452014
penalties.details: The Company received notice for conducting audit under Section 65 of the CGST Act, 2017, from the Office of the Assistant Commissioner (Audit), CGST & Central Excise (Audit), Circle-V, 1st Floor, Indore, M.P.-452014, on April 17, 2025. During the audit, certain observations were raised via ADT-02 dated January 19, 2026 allegingwrong availment of blocked credit under Section 17(5) of the CGST Act, 2017 and issuance of credit notes at 28% GST without corresponding supply during the relevant period. Pursuant to the above, the Company have deposited the demand of Rs 3,25,442 including penalty of Rs. 24,375/- under IGST, Rs. 2,605/- under CGST and Rs. 2,605/- under SGST through Form DRC-03 on February 13, 2026
penalties.impact: The matter stands concluded and audit proceedings have been closed.. The Company does not expect any material financial impact arising therefrom.

penalties.authority: The Office of Assistant Commissioner, State Tax Durg Circle -1. Durg (C.G.), Chhattisgarh
penalties.details: The Company received a Show Cause Notice dated March 6, 2026, under Section 74 of the CGST Act, 2017 for FY 2023-24, alleging wrongful availment of ITC from a non-existing firm, The Company had claimed the ITC on the basis of valid invoices, and supportingpayment proof; however to avoid litigation, the Company accepted the demand of Rs 3,981 including penalty of Rs 200 each under CGST & SGST through Form DRC-03 on March 19, 2026
penalties.impact: The matter stands concluded. and the Company does not expect any material financial impact arising therefrom.

penalties.authority: Office of the Commercial Tax Officer, Ward-7, Chandigarh
penalties.details: In furtherance to the disclosure made in the previous quarter ( Q3 – FY 2025-26) regarding a demand notice dated December 26, 2025 issued by the Commercial Tax Officer, Chandigarh, under Section 73 of the CGST Act, 2017 for FY 2021–22, the Company had filed a rectification application against the order dated February 2, 2026 on account of incorrect computation of penalty. The said rectification application was accepted by the department on March 24, 2026 , pursuant to which the penalty has been reduced to Rs. 5,000/- under CGST and Rs. 5,000/- under SGST. Accordingly, the Company has deposited the revised penalty amount aggregating to Rs. 10,000/- through Form DRC-03 dated March 24, 2026
penalties.impact: The matter stands concluded. and the Company does not expect any material financial impact arising therefrom.

penalties.authority: Office of the Joint Commissioner (ST), Intelligence-I, Chennai - 600006
penalties.details: Further to the disclosure made for the quarter ended December 31,2025, the appeal filed by the Company on January 2, 2026 against the penalty imposed under Section 129 of the CGST Act, 2017, in relation to the detention of goods during transit, has been decided in favour of the Company vide appellate order dated September 28, 2026. The appellate authority has set aside the entire tax and other demand liabilities, except for a penalty of Rs. 10,000/- under CGST and Rs. 10,000/- under SGST. The Company had deposited a penalty of Rs. 2,27,775/- under CGST and Rs. 2,27,775/- under SGST under protest vide Form DRC-03 dated November 18, 2025 to secure the release of the goods. In view of the favourable appellate order, the Company had filed a refund application for the amount refundable in accordance with the said order.
penalties.impact: The appellate authority has set aside the tax and other demand liabilities, retaining a penalty of Rs. 10,000/- under CGST and Rs. 10,000/- under SGST. The Company had filed a refund application for the pre deposit amount of Rs 2,27,775 under CGST and SGST after adjusting confirmed penalty amount.

operating_notes.text: CRISIL assigned Crisil A/Stable long-term and Crisil A1 short-term ratings to ₹325 Cr bank loan facilities of material wholly owned subsidiary AIL Dixon Technologies Private Limited.
Utilised ₹375 Cr of IPO proceeds for debt repayment and ₹90 Cr for general corporate purposes as of March 31, 2026.
Customs demand of ₹30.86 Cr (including penalties) on 4G routers is being contested at CESTAT.
Construction at Noida Sector 135 site is in advanced stages with ₹61.68 Cr incurred as of March 2026.
Incorporated wholly owned subsidiary Aditya Infotech Taiwan Co. Limited on February 02, 2026 for R&D.
Market share reached ~45.4% in Q3 FY26 in India's organized video surveillance industry.
CP PLUS contributed 86% of overall revenue in FY26, with IP products comprising 73% of the brand's portfolio.
Cash conversion cycle improved to 64 days due to reduction in inventory and debtor days
CP PLUS brand contributed 87% of total revenue, with IP products making up 79% of CP PLUS portfolio
BOM consists of 55-60% imported components (35% semiconductors from Taiwan, 15-20% passive electronics from Taiwan/China)
Appointed Ranveer Singh as Brand Ambassador for CP PLUS

timeline.summary: CRISIL assigned Crisil A/Stable and A1 ratings to ₹325 Cr bank facilities of subsidiary AIL Dixon Technologies.
Aditya Infotech received an administrative warning letter from SEBI concerning compliance with PIT Regulations on May 7, 2026.
Aditya Infotech Limited’s officials will attend an investor/analyst visit at its Andhra Pradesh subsidiary plant on May 15, 2026, from 10:00 AM.
Aditya Infotech reported the full utilisation of ₹375 Cr from IPO proceeds for debt repayment as of March 31, 2026.
Aditya Infotech Limited’s Roshni Tandon (A21150) schedules Q4 & FY26 results conference call on May 28, 2026, at 12:30 PM IST with MD Aditya Khemka, Director Anup Nair, and CFO Yogesh Sharma.
Q4FY26 consolidated revenue at ₹1,422 Cr with PAT tripling to ₹169 Cr; board recommended ₹1.64 dividend.
Aditya Infotech Limited held earnings conference call on May 28, 2026, at 12:30 IST to discuss audited financial results for Q4FY26 and FY26, with audio recording uploaded.
Aditya Infotech raised FY27 revenue guidance to ₹6,000-6,500 Cr and EBITDA margins to 14-15% during its Q4FY26 earnings call.
Aditya Infotech appointed actor Ranveer Singh as the Brand Ambassador for its CP PLUS brand.

watchlist.response: Aditya Infotech is using purchasing scale to secure forward supplies directly from multiple fab and chipset makers, passing on costs via monthly price hikes.
watchlist.text: Global memory (DDR3) and SoC shortages squeezing input costs and stretching working capital.

watchlist.response: Management is gradually passing price increases to customers (15-20% taken in H1, 25% expected for FY27) and maintains FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 14-15%
watchlist.text: Sustainability of margins given exhaustion of low-cost inventory and ongoing semiconductor price escalations

watchlist.response: Company has transitioned away from Chinese components over 1.5 years, with 40+ brands now certified; supply chain challenges are better mitigated by larger organizations
